html:
SMTO-EXE-0005 — A command ran too long and SMTO stopped it

GUID: 9bae767e-8532-45f3-bc03-b76598e58dab
Slug: foreground-execution-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • A command in your task hit the time limit for commands that run while you wait, so SMTO stopped it. Anything it changed before it was stopped may still be in place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task in the conversation and read the stopped command's output. Then check on that computer whether the files or programs it was changing are already done. The command may have finished part of its work, and running it again from the start could repeat those changes.
  2. If the work really needs more time, open Settings › Agent behavior › Advanced and choose a longer Maximum foreground runtime. This is the limit the command hit; the new value only applies to commands started after you change it.
  3. Or ask SMTO in the conversation to give the command more time, run it as a background job, or split it into smaller steps that each finish sooner. SMTO may have set a shorter limit for this one command; background jobs aren't bound by this limit, and smaller steps finish well within it.

What success looks like

  • The command finishes and the task shows its result instead of a time-limit message.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If the command stopped well before the limit you chose, the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) may have its own shorter limit. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up that Gateway. Don't raise other, unrelated limits.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A foreground command was terminated after reaching its effective time limit (the Maximum foreground runtime ceiling, a shorter timeout requested for the command, the run's remaining deadline, or the Gateway's own execution limit), and its receipt was recorded as timed_out.

What this means

  • Runtime-owned execution facts show that the foreground process reached its configured execution allowance; a cancellation receipt can also be classified as timeout when the local timeout flag was set. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Runtime-owned execution facts show that the foreground process reached its configured execution allowance; a cancellation receipt can also be classified as timeout when the local timeout flag was set.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the terminal process state, timeout fact and retained output; distinguish this execution limit from the model request timeout.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the operation receipt (process_state=timed_out, effective_timeout_seconds, timeout_source: configured_absolute_ceiling, model, run_deadline or gateway_execution_limit) and the command's partial effects before rerunning anything. For legitimately long work, raise max_foreground_execution_seconds (Settings › Agent behavior › Advanced › Maximum foreground runtime, 5 minutes–24 hours, applies to new operations), request a longer timeout for the command, or run it as a background job; if timeout_source is gateway_execution_limit, raise GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS on that Gateway (0 disables it) instead of changing unrelated limits.
  • Inspect the command outcome and reduce its scope. For legitimately long foreground work, adjust Maximum foreground runtime under Advanced for new operations or use the supported background job flow.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Maximum Foreground Runtime: advanced / max_foreground_execution_seconds. Applies to: new operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original process and effects are settled, and any justified new work fits its execution allowance or supported background lifecycle.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-LLM-0001 — Model request timed out
  • SMTO-LLM-0037 — An older retry attempt ran out of time
  • SMTO-CTX-0001 — The AI model said your request was too long for it
  • SMTO-LLM-0015 — The model ran out of room before finishing its reply
